bearings.system_side: office_moves are directed consecutive-span pairs, emitted with SEQUENCE IS NOT A SOCIAL EDGE and canonical_eligible False. The paper's tie is not a sequence link: it is the undirected co-service count, whose closest analogue in the system is shared_with / pair_people, which has no window. The rule against treating sequence as a person-person edge is still consistent with the paper's caution about homophily.

bearings.system_side: Access-uncertainty cost uses a fixed 5-year staleness half-life on years since last joint overlap (staleness = ln2 * age / 5). The file labels its calibration as 'Exploratory log-cost scenarios; not fitted success or friendship probabilities', and the docstring calls the costs assumptions that must not be shown as probabilities.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Weak. The paper's window concerns member-member outcome similarity, not whether staffer-staffer relationships remain usable. It cannot calibrate the half-life.
bearings.verifier_note: Window interval and the not-a-decay-estimate caveat verified in the text. Code constants, staleness formula and exploratory label verified. The code does not claim calibration, so no change needed.

summary_issues: Calls Montgomery's tie an office-to-office sequence link that the system emits as directed moves. The paper's W is an undirected, row-standardized co-service count over the current and two prior Congresses (p.11, fn 12, p.18). Sequence is the theory, not the operational tie.
States the window as 1997-2010. The text gives only the 105th-111th Congresses and never states years; 1997-2010 is calendar arithmetic.

Says the senior ideology result shows nothing (-0.003). Strictly, the paper says only that it is not reliably distinguishable from zero (95% CI -0.029 to 0.020); Table 3 has 4 of 7 Congress estimates positive, so the summary's flat reading is a fair shorthand but not a finding of no effect.
